extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF/OA figures; automated placeholders were replaced.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: P5 and the truncated peptides disrupt bacterial membranes, supported by PI uptake in P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 and S. aureus ATCC 25923 and NPN uptake in P. aeruginosa.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Fig. 5 supports qualitative/relative permeability changes; exact curve values are not text-tabulated and are not fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides induce cytoplasmic membrane depolarization, with P. aeruginosa showing fluorescence increases over time and S. aureus depolarization except weaker P5-CT2/P5-CT3 behavior.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Depolarization is retained as direct membrane-mechanism evidence; exact per-curve fluorescence values are not tabulated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FACS PI-positive cell percentages after 2x MIC treatment support membrane integrity loss, with stronger effects for P5, P5-CT1, and P5-NT1 than for shorter truncations.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source text contains selected PI-positive percentages; this does not by itself quantify all membrane assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectra in membrane-mimic environments and in LTA/LPS support amphipathic helical interaction context, but this is supporting structure/interaction evidence rather than a standalone killing mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Structure of Peptides in Various Environments;xml:fig=1

mechanism_claims.limitations: CD/LTA/LPS data are not promoted to direct killing mechanism without permeability/depolarization assays.

quality_controls.overclaim_guard: CD/LTA/LPS and biofilm context are not promoted beyond supporting evidence.

caution_findings.note: Source text provides selected FACS percentages and qualitative trends; unreported graph values are not fabricated.
